sentences.span: oil prices are somewhat elevated but refined product prices (and crack spreads) are near record levels
sentences.why: Source states the exact split the sentence describes: crude itself only elevated, refined product/crack spreads at records, i.e. the two have decoupled.

sentences.span: Markets seem to only react badly when actual events affecting energy prices occur. Markets seem to react positively to any story, rumor, or hope that is positive.
sentences.why: Academy Securities states directly that positive rumors/hope reprice energy markets, matching the sentence's mechanism.

sentences.span: remove that shock absorber and GIR says fair value is roughly $10-15 higher
sentences.why: The only 'fair value' oil call in the source set is Goldman Sachs's GIR (Jared Cohen), not JPMorgan. Attribution changed to a different bank.

sentences.span: we are hard-pressed to see a resolution to energy price pressures anytime soon and incorporate features of a higher oil risk-premium into the baseline
sentences.why: Morgan Stanley's actual view is that the oil risk premium is durable/structural (they moved it into their baseline), not 'already fading' as the sentence asserts.

sentences.span: GIR says fair value is roughly $10-15 higher... On the Trump-Xi meeting, the only thing that matters is any signal Xi is shifting away from 'playing for time'
sentences.why: The Trump-Xi/oil-premium linkage traces to Goldman's Jared Cohen (fair value $10-15, not $16), not JPMorgan; the BofA short-2yr-Treasury/$SHY claim has no support anywhere in the source set.
This is a claim about the pulse's own prior trade call from 'last Monday' — an internal publication history fact, not something any source PDF could support.

sentences.span: HYPERSCALER FREE CASH FLOW TURNS NEGATIVE FROM 4Q26 ONWARDS
sentences.why: Corroborated by 17233 (hyperscaler IG debt issuance estimates raised to $400-420bn for 2027) and 17166 (AI debt issuance discussed as competing with duration supply and affecting yields) — FCF shortfall funded by bond issuance, tied to yields.
No source frames an internal counter-argument as originating 'from inside the same houses'; the adjacent claim it bridges to (s9) is itself fabricated.
No document in the source set mentions a BofA fund manager survey, an 'overinvesting' figure, or Goldman semiconductor gross-margin statistics of 70%/55%.

sentences.span: Markets are now pricing in a greater than 50% chance of a hike in October and three more hikes this cycle
sentences.why: Source says odds lean toward a hike ('greater than 50%'), not an even 'coin flip' — the sentence flattens a tilted probability into a toss-up.

sentences.span: it's hard to not look at two-year yields approaching 4.75% and say they are attractive
sentences.why: Consistent with 17157's '2-year Treasury yield rose... to 4.7%'; 4.744% falls between the two reported figures, and the October-hike-odds logic is sourced.

sentences.span: In the US, funds sold Semis, broader AI Tech, Discretionary and Industrials / Energy exposures, while adding to Hyperscalers, Optical Networking, Cybersecurity, Financials and Materials
sentences.why: The semis-to-financials flow is real but describes one week of hedge-fund positioning (as of Thursday), not a trend running 'since the Nasdaq peaked in early June'; GS Coppersmith (17230) separately shows Tech as the most net-bought US sector for three straight weeks, and no source mentions a June Nasdaq peak.

GS Coppersmith (17230) documents deteriorating breadth (<30% of S&P above the 50-day average) alongside index resilience, but no source characterizes this as 'not panic selling' or 'what a market top looks like' — that specific interpretive framing isn't any bank's stated stance.

sentences.span: The BoJ delivered a 25bp rate hike, citing rising upside inflation risks. Sato and Asada dissented in favour of no policy change
sentences.why: The 1.25% level and two named dissenters (Sato, Asada) are confirmed, but no source states a 7-2 vote count, calls 1.25% the highest since 1995, or says either dissenter was appointed by PM Takaichi — those specifics are invented additions.

sentences.span: The US August inflation reports came in above expectations, with core inflation accelerating by 0.3% month-on-month versus the 0.2% consensus forecast
sentences.why: Sources describe the August print as a hawkish surprise (above expectations, cited by 17189 as a 'swing factor' for the hike), the opposite of the sentence's claim that it came in benign/below-expectations and 'does not force the next move'; no source gives a January 2027 UBS/Goldman hike call.
